hook.en: Douglas ends his story by saying that he had learnt something deeper than swimming. What did his struggle teach him about fear itself?

objectives.en: Identify the main themes of Deep Water
Explain the message about the fear of fear
Relate the lesson to your own life

narration.en: Douglas ends his story by saying that he had learnt something deeper than swimming. What did his struggle teach him about fear itself?

body.en: The central theme is fear and the courage needed to overcome it. Douglas shows that fear, once allowed to grow, can limit an entire life, but that will power, patience and proper guidance can defeat it. The story also shows the value of small, steady steps instead of one dramatic leap.

points.en: Fear and how it grows when avoided
Patience: one skill at a time
Freedom that comes from facing fear

say.en: At the centre is fear, and the courage to face it.
Douglas learnt that the real enemy was the fear of fear itself.
He used his will power to fight back.
He learnt patiently, one skill at a time.
A good instructor made the difference.
He tested himself again and again to be sure.
In the end he won freedom and joy.

explanation.en: Being released from fear gave Douglas a stronger will to live with courage.

body.en: Douglas says that the terror he felt was really a fear of fear itself, and that he now understood what it means to be released from it. He recalls Franklin D. Roosevelt's idea that all we have to fear is fear itself. Having conquered this fear, he felt free to enjoy life fully, and the experience gave him a will to live with more courage.

A lesson for life, not only for swimming

problem.en: What can students learn from Douglas's experience about facing their own fears?

steps.en: Name the lesson: fears do not vanish by avoiding them.
Give the method: face the fear in small, guided, regular steps.
Give the reward: confidence and freedom in other parts of life.

answer.en: Douglas shows that avoiding a fear only makes it grow. By facing it step by step with guidance and will power, as he did with swimming, students can overcome fears such as stage fright and gain confidence and freedom.
